analysis: Only scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py changed: a unit-test file with no runtime or provider code. It adds WATCHDOG = "darkbloom-watchdog.yml" (head lines 69-71) and allows that workflow in test_every_workflow_is_classified (line 463). The self-hosted/darkbloom label ban now exempts the watchdog (lines 579-580). It adds test_watchdog_rescues_only_this_repositorys_routed_runs (lines 591-617). That test pins the watchdog's properties: schedule/workflow_dispatch triggers only, top-level permissions {}, runs-on ubuntu-24.04, job permissions limited to actions:write and checks:write, no uses/secrets/checkout/id-token/contents, API calls scoped to $REPOSITORY, and action only on runs with a queued darkbloom-labelled self-hosted job. It also asserts that release, signing and credentialed (UNROUTED) workflows carry no darkbloom or self-hosted runners. These assertions tighten the CI guardrails and do not weaken them. The exemption for the watchdog is narrow (exact filename), and the watchdog itself is not constrained from naming the labels beyond the other assertions. The watchdog workflow file is not in the supplied evidence. Its actual content, and whether actions:write permission and the cancel/re-run behavior are safe, are unverified here. That is a CI concern outside the provider threat-model assets (TB-002 to TB-013 cover provider runtime, not CI). No threat-model assets, trust boundaries or mitigations (A-001 to A-019, T-041 and others) are affected. The head and base views line up with the stated ranges. The patch excerpt is truncated but the head text is fully visible. No finding. A follow-up reviewer could examine .github/workflows/darkbloom-watchdog.yml directly.
